rationale:
structural: `requirements.sdk.graph.validation-context.outgoing_edges.mcp.description` only fixes the description text of the `outgoing_edges` MCP tool: "Inspect a known node's outgoing targets for the requested label, making those targets available to read_node." That is observable output. It names no library, algorithm, signature, type, field or delegation through a named interface. The same string could come from a constant, a separate helper, or a differently shaped JSON literal. Clients would see the same tool description, so the clause is satisfied either way. No structural obligation needs implementation evidence.

The supplied root, `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/tools.rs#impl[GraphSession<'_, '_, D>/Conversation]/fn[tools]`, does emit an `outgoing_edges` tool definition with this exact description string. It already carries the `{impl}` marker, so nothing is missing.

behavioral: The requirement `requirements.sdk.graph.validation-context.outgoing_edges.mcp.description` has one observable obligation. The published `outgoing_edges` tool's description must be exactly: "Inspect a known node's outgoing targets for the requested label, making those targets available to read_node."

`crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/tests.rs#fn[published_tool_descriptions_match_the_contract]` is marked `{test}` for this requirement. It finds the tool named `outgoing_edges` and uses `assert_eq!` to compare its `description` to the exact required string. A wrong, missing or altered description would fail this assertion.

The requirement states no other behavior, and I found no other obligation that needs a test. I did not read any implementation source.
